name: Customer Voice
focus: Mine reviews, complaints, objections and unmet needs
summary: Material change: Kit Muda Cero should be positioned by coat and surface, not as universal. Slicker suitability depends on coat type and technique; reusable rollers are strongest on flat textiles but weaker on clothing, leather and slick surfaces.

insights.insight: Slicker suitability depends on coat type, pin length, pressure and repeated passes; misuse can cause irritation or brush burn.
insights.action: Add coat-type suitability and safe-use guidance; avoid universal claims.

insights.insight: Reusable pet-hair rollers perform best on sofas, bedding and fabric car seats, while clothing, leather and slick surfaces are recurring misses.
insights.action: Narrow the promise to textiles and demonstrate the back-and-forth technique.

insights.insight: Fit, clip/zipper durability, waterproof-backing wear and sliding are the main quality/return risks.
insights.action: Require exact dimensions, reinforced hardware, seat anchors and wash durability; avoid vague universal-fit claims.

insights.insight: Seat protection is a strong benefit, but the hammock or bundled tether should not be treated as crash protection.
insights.action: Separate cleanliness/containment claims from restraint-safety claims.

insights.insight: Convenience and compact storage are the primary desire; wrong size, weak handles/ribs and mirror/dashboard interference drive objections.
insights.action: Prefer multi-size variants with flexible/padded handles and a measure-before-buy fit guide.

creative_offer: Make Kit Muda Cero a coat/surface-specific 3-step routine.
Do not hero clothes or leather for the reusable roller.
Use prevention plus cleanup, not one-tool-does-all messaging.
store_builder: Add a tool-by-coat/surface matrix near the bundle demo.
If the car-cover challenger advances, add vehicle measurement guidance.
compliance: Do not imply crash protection for dog hammocks without evidence.
